The Oyo State Government has handed over 88 newly reconstructed shops to traders affected by a fire outbreak at Alesinloye Market in Ibadan. The Executive Chairman of Ibadan South-West Local Government, Kehinde Akande, performed the handover on Wednesday on behalf of Governor Seyi Makinde. Akande said the exercise fulfilled a promise made by the governor during his visit to the market after the fire incident. The inferno, which occurred in the plastic and rubber section of the market, destroyed several shops and goods worth millions of naira. Speaking at the ceremony, Akande said the government had promised to rebuild the affected shops and return them to the traders free of charge. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. We came here to sympathise with the victims and assure them that the government would reconstruct the affected section of the market. “Our governor, as we all know, is a man of the people. Whenever anything happens in the state, he is always present. He promised that the shops would be rebuilt and handed back to the victims free of charge, and that is what we are doing today.” In a statement issued by the governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju, Akande described the handover as a significant milestone for the market community. Akande also announced measures to prevent a recurrence of the incident, including the rebuilding of the market’s fire station and the permanent deployment of local government safety officers to monitor compliance with safety regulations. He said the state government had earlier paid each affected trader N250,000 as immediate relief to cushion the impact of the losses. “When the incident happened, both state and local government officials visited the market to sympathise with the traders. After the Deputy Governor’s visit, the Governor himself came here and immediately approved the payment of N250,000 to each affected trader to help alleviate their losses,” he said. A former member of the House of Representatives, Saheed Akinade-Fijabi, described the handover as evidence of the governor’s commitment to fulfilling his promises. He urged the beneficiaries to maintain the facilities and use them responsibly, adding that the 88 shops corresponded with the number of traders on the verified list compiled after the fire outbreak. Speaking on behalf of the traders, Taiwo Sekinat Bisola, who represented the Babaloja of Alesinloye Market, thanked the state government for the gesture. She described the intervention as a major relief that had restored the affected traders’ means of livelihood and urged beneficiaries to maintain the shops and observe safety measures.The fire broke out in the early hours of March 11, 2026, in the plastic and rubber section of Alesinloye Market, destroying shops and goods worth millions of naira.
